Nothing hits like Tender! The first time I ever heard them was when I stumbled across “Slow Love” one sad day and I was in sweet, uncontrollable tears within seconds! I don’t think that’s ever happened to me in my life… Where I was brought to tears immediately after hearing a song for the first time…. And it wasn’t because of the terrible day I was having; it was because that song pierced through my hard exterior and made sense of the maddening anguish in my heart. It perfectly describes my past relationship that I still feel nostalgic and yet resentful about. For the first time in a long time, I found a perfect convergence of all the emotions & epiphanies I was feeling that gave me the most enrapturing, full-bodied auricular experience. That’s why I made a point to travel 90 miles, despite not having much money for gas, to go see them live when they recently visited the States. And, just as I expected, they captivated my soul immediately. And they were gracious enough to stick around after the show to meet a long line of fans, including myself. I was pretty nervous at the time so I didn't really know what to say to the ones who brought some light back into the ominous darkness brought on by the erosion of life. I was also having a very sad day that day too, but just like the last time, Tender whispered their raw, humbling lyrics into my soul and lifted my entire being with their nectarous melodies. It reduced me to a position of  subservience that was beautiful and meaningful. That’s what I really wanted to tell them when I met them, but the words escaped me when I was presented with the opportunity. I honestly cannot wait to see them again and I would stop at nothing to get there. You have a fan for life, Tender! Thank you so much for what you’ve created and for taking the time to meet your fans that day! I hope to meet you again and wish you all the success you deserve!

songs.song: Extended, ADHD Focus Music, ADHD Music Therapy, Isochronic Tones
songs.comment_text:
I am 66 yrs old and was recently told by my Doctor that I have been living with undiagnosed ADHD all of my life. I can tell you a couple of things about my life, it has been Amazing! I followed my own interests. I never let people's judgements convince me that I was something I wasn't or allow myself to become someone whose self belief and worth depended on other people's opinions of me.
I had different interests from most of my classmates as a kid, but I explored my interests by myself or occasionally with someone I might meet who shared an interest or two with me. I never ignored my own path to follow the crowd and although I was thrilled to meet someone who shared some interest or hobby with me, I was never disappointed or feeling left out by the crowd. I always liked being me, even though sometimes it seemed as though just being yourself draws all kinds of criticism and even insults from others, there was Nothing in my life that I would have traded just to fit in with the crowd. When I was a kid in school, we were strapped for very many small and unjustifiable reasons, I know now that the main reason was for the teacher's purpose, they had no other tool in their toolbox that they could use to establish Crowd Control of a classroom full of kids.
These days, I believe, that the teachers position has not gifted them with any new tools to replace that Strap they've been deprived of and since kids are still kids and teachers are still dealing with exactly the same problems as they did in years gone by, I believe they've been making their lives easier by talking to parents and Doctors about their problem, which is. They believe themselves to be Great Teachers as they were Great Students but who would believe that when so many kids are floundering in School?
Their own sense of self preservation, I think, has led them to claim that while they are Great teachers despite the numbers of children and students who fail, it's simply because those kids "Just can't Learn"
Why would that be? Because they just can't focus on the drivel the curriculum forces me to teach them one and all, when no two think alike...that's what I think has become the conversation talking points....the teachers are great, the curriculum is scintillatingly interesting but half of the kids just can't seem to Focus on most of the subjects long enough to learn, they start fidgeting and doodling (out of boredom?) and distract the rest of the class.
Then the parents teacher day causes stress in all of the Parents, they get the suggestion that their kid should maybe be seen and tested for ADHD and sure enough, the next thing you know, half the kids or more and all being medicated to get along in their classes.
I'm starting to think that the old strap was a lot easier on our minds than the diagnosis and medications have been on yours.
When some teacher strapped me, in the back of my mind, I always thought that there was something wrong with that teacher doing that to us kids.
These days, after you've been seen and told any of a multitude of things are Wrong With You and you have been duly medicated and left believing that something was wrong with You. that's a Horrible thing to plant in a young persons mind.
We had a lot of violence to live with and a lot of hard work to do, but we never heard of kids suffering from anxiety or panic attacks or needing to be medicated to allow us to focus on many things that no kid in it's right mind would want to spend two minutes focusing on.
Make sure that you don't take all the judgements and labels to heart, Believe in yourself, you've got two arms and two legs like everyone else and you can do whatever anyone else can, as long as You really want to.
If you don't believe me, check it out, a great number of successful people, really successful people have been told they have ADHD, including most of those who work in Silicon Valley, some of the most famous techie names you ever heard of, they got so good at something because they were great at focusing on that thing, which could be all about computers or programming, or observing nature or farming, or painting, or anything at all.
Don't let being "different" cause you to look at yourself in any way other than as an Original Masterpiece. Those are not always recognized immediately by the masses, but once they are, they can often go from being shunned to being adored, look at Van Gough and many many others, what they went through just because they were different and nobody was able to recognize their greatness, that wasn't their fault, it didn't make them less great, they believed in themselves, not what others thought about them. You Do that Too, if you don't do anything else, Get your own back!

songs.song: You're a Detective in the 1940s on a Rainy Night | Calm Jazz Music for Foggy Nights
songs.comment_text:
I was posted outside a warehouse on Pier 9—the kind of place where bodies go missing and questions get answered with silence.
I had a name, a lead, and a snub-nosed .38 that still smelled like the last mistake I didn’t regret.

Then she showed up.
Red coat. Black heels. Hair like spilled ink. She moved through the rain like she owned it—like the whole night was her stage, and I was the fool with a front-row ticket.

“You’re late,” I said.
She lit a cigarette, lips painted in lies. “You’re early,” she replied. “That’s what gets men killed in this town.”

Behind her—tires squealed. A black sedan—no lights, no plates—came sliding around the corner.
My hand was already on the steel before the doors flew open.

Three suits. One problem. No place to run that didn’t end in blood.

songs.song: Sound bath for positive energy change
songs.comment_text:
Thank you Travis. As an empath. Life can be overwhelming. It seems almost selfish to do any self care. The goal is always to press on. Someone will always need you, be grateful for you, become inspired because of you. It's my belief we are here to help each other, for the collective good, but not at the cost of ourselves. Tonight I Thank you for the gift of music, talent and time. I am lying on the floor snuggled with a blanket. Listening to this. As if a pause. As if, I hear and feel nothing else except me. Who tragically has been neglected, in these last weeks. The one person I forgot to care for while caring for others.

For anyone who is reading this. Treat yourself, the way you treat others. Buy yourself flowers, take yourself shopping, go get that sweet treat. Do one nice thing for yourself and someone else today.

Also give back while taking, and that includes yourself. You are beautiful. You are love. And you are loved just the way you are.

I wish something really good happens to everyone today. Remember this won't last forever, like seasons, one must end and a new will begin. Death js an opportunity at a rebirth of something. Suffering is not for nothing. You can do hard things. This too shall pass. Please never give up, sit, take a break if you must, but keep going! ❤

With all my ❤
Stephanie

When I was 16, after 10 years of compulsory public education, I watched a couple of friends leave to further their tertiary educations overseas, while I could only get a local polytechnic diploma. 2-3 years after that, I watch more friends walk proudly into various local universities, while my educational journey came to an end. I came from a poor family and my father could only send me for basic education and nothing more as I had 3 younger siblings who were still schooling. After 3 years in the military, I began working and became the family bread winner. I never stopped working for almost 25 years and slowly climbed up the career ladder. A few years ago, I hear this song and it struck a cord in me. I decided it was time. I enrolled in graduate school at 45. Next to the lecturer, I was the oldest person in class. Everywhere I went on campus, I stood out like a sore thumb. Everyone was on laptops and tablets, while I was on books, papers and pencils. But I didn't give up, I kept turning to this song to keep me going. THIS was MY fight song. I struggled hard but help soon came. Classmates half my age who once spurred the 'old dude' from groups in class, turned to me for life advice and in turn, helped me navigate the digital world and gadgets and online submissions. I still turned to this song to keep the fire going when I wanted to give up.

I graduated last year, ahead of schedule, 4 years out of a 5 year part time degree programme. My parents couldn't make it as they were too frail. There was no one in the audience clapping for a 49 year old graduate. But I was proud. I had made it. And this song was one of those songs that just kept me telling myself ... I can do this!

I’m 53 years old and something similar happened to me when I was younger.  Billie is so young and I usually don’t relate with songs by much younger artists.  But boy does this hit home.  This song is haunting and I can’t get it out of my head.  I just keep listening to it over and over. I actually came upon this song by accident...I’m glad I did.

this song is one of few that makes me feel that life is worth living. ive been in a slump of depression and self hate the past week or so, then i came across this song. i realized i can and i will get better. to people like me out there listening, i want you to know its okay to feel like this. its okay to cry yourself to sleep every night for weeks, because just know youll be okay at some point.
i didnt think i'd make it to 13 but i did. im still here, and you can make it too. take my hand when you're ready, i'll wait. i wont force you to get better, i know its hard.
